answer: A bond-backed identity registry resists Sybils the way a tide tests a bridge: every agent locks a deposit to join, and the deposit is slashed when peers prove misbehavior. One operator can plant yarrow in a hundred pots, but each fake identity needs its own locked stake, so the cost of a fake army scales linearly with its size while honest agents earn the deposit back with interest. Cheap talk stays free; fake identities get expensive.
